summary: Host work posted by the device and joined inside a CUDA stream or captured graph, with a measured choice of wait
implementation_scope: C++/CUDA mailbox over caller-owned mapped pinned memory: device-reset doorbells (done = 0 before ready = 1, survive graph replay), device-answered skips, host service thread, stream-front-end and poll-kernel joins plus an eager host join, release with a sweeper for stuck windows, rearm, terminal failure answering, functional support probe and replayed-graph join cost measurement; Python host reference of the protocol. Payload layout, handler arithmetic and worker pools remain engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: A graph-captured step needs host computation or host-issued work that the device decides on at run time (host-computed experts, host lookups, copies), and splitting the graph with a host synchronization per decision costs too much
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The host work is known before launch, fits on the device, or the measured join cost exceeds the work moved; never assume the stream wait is free on a platform without measuring it
provides: Per-slot ready/done/status words and payload laid over a caller-owned mapped region
Device-side post and skip helpers that reset done before raising ready, so captured joins wait for a constant
Stream-front-end join (cuStreamWaitValue32 resolved through the runtime) and one-thread poll-kernel join on the same word
Eager host join for platforms without a capturable join, rejecting capture
Service thread answering doorbells in any order; release() with a sweeper that drains stuck windows; rearm() after drained streams
Terminal failure: every later doorbell answered at once with status failed and the handler never called again
Functional probe of stream-wait support, eagerly and captured, and per-join cost measured in a replayed graph
engine_supplies: Mapped pinned bytes allocated and accounted through Core (CudaBackend host buffers or cuda_map_host)
Payload layout, system-fenced payload writes before each post, and volatile reads of results after the join
The handler and any worker pool it uses; handlers must return
Join choice from measure_joins on the target machine, ideally re-checked within the engine's own step
Watchdog or cancellation calling release(), and discarding outputs of windows whose status is released or failed
preserve: The device resets done before raising ready, after a system fence over the payload
The host writes status before done; done >= 1 is the only completion signal
One outstanding job per slot until the stream has joined it
Slots without host work are answered by the device (skip) so every captured join completes
Failure is terminal and answers every later doorbell; rearm only after every joining stream is drained
adapt: Slot count, payload layout and posting from a kernel or a stream operation
Join kind by measured cost; polling and back-off policy of the service
Handler threading and how results are reduced on the device

code_files.purpose: Mailbox, slot views, join kinds, release/rearm/failure contract, probe and cost measurement
Post/skip/poll kernels, stream wait through a runtime-resolved driver entry point, service and sweeper threads, probe and measurement
Device-side post, skip and result reads for engine kernels
Host reference of the protocol with captured programs replayed in order

requires.hardware: A CUDA device that maps pinned host memory; the stream-wait join additionally needs driver support for 32-bit stream memory operations on mapped memory, probed at run time. Python 3.11+ for the host reference
requires.model: Any model; the payload and handler are engine defined
requires.workload: Graph-captured or eager steps with host work decided on the device

contract.input: Caller-owned mapped region of region_bytes(slots, payload), slot count, payload bytes, join kind and handler; device posts with system-fenced payloads
contract.output: Per slot a status (served, skipped, failed, released) and the handler's payload outputs, visible to the stream after its join
contract.ownership: The caller keeps the mapped region and its accounting alive past the mailbox; the stream reads results only after the join; one outstanding job per slot
contract.failure: A throwing handler fails the mailbox for good and answers every later doorbell with status failed; release() answers pending and later doorbells with status released; rearm() refuses while a job runs or after failure; the eager join rejects capture and reports a join of an unposted slot
contract.core_boundary: Engines allocate the region through Core resources and include release() in drain and cancellation; Core is not changed

dependencies: Python standard library for the host reference

validation.host: Worked example covers replayed captured programs, the stale answer without a device reset, release, rearm and terminal failure
validation.native: CUDA fixture (RTX 5090; native Windows and WSL2) replays an eight-slot window 200 times with both capturable joins and a skipped slot, releases a window held by a stuck job, fails the handler on the fifth job, serves an aborted window's doorbells, posts in reverse order, and checks the eager join and its capture rejection
validation.performance: Post plus join on one RTX 5090 (driver 596.49) was 37-41 us with stream_wait and 2.7-2.8 us with device_poll on native Windows and WSL2. In one MoE engine on that machine (WSL2, about 40 joins per pass) device_poll matched the engine's own spin handshake (33.8 vs 33.0 tok/s speculative decode, identical output) and stream_wait cost about 8% of plain decode
